ViolationDescription: Conflation of read-only presentation hydration with authoritative Go scene mutation. Calling setLoadedPhoto dispatches Background.Set to Go, bumping revision during history undo, project load, and post-commit updates.
ActualCallPath: HistoryManager.undo() -> window.setLoadedPhoto() (app.js:6656) -> SceneState.setLoadedPhoto() (scene-state.js:137) -> EngineBridge.setBackground() (engine-bridge.js:1636) -> Background.Set -> activeScene.SetBackground() (scene.go:1016)
FailureScenario: History undo/redo of background changes mutates Go scene revision; project load dispatches duplicate Background.Set commands; rejected Go background mutations leave JS displaying uncommitted pixels.
RemediationProposal: Decouple presentation hydration (e.g. hydrateBackgroundPresentation) from state mutation. Suppress bridge dispatch when setLoadedPhoto is invoked during history restore or project hydration.
RegressionTestRequired: Verify HistoryManager.undo does not emit Background.Set commands across bridge and does not advance Go scene revision.

ViolationDescription: Timeline frame evaluation bypasses Go WASM evaluator in fresh sessions because _sceneSynced is initialized to false and only set to true inside syncScene(), which is only called during project loading.
ActualCallPath: Page load -> EngineBridge.init() (isReady=true, _sceneSynced=false) -> TimelinePlayer._loop() -> evaluateSceneAtTime(t) -> checks _sceneSynced (false) -> executes _evaluateSceneAtTimeJS() (380 lines of shadow JS timeline math)
FailureScenario: Fresh editor sessions without prior project loads run the JavaScript shadow timeline math rather than the authoritative Go timeline engine; animation curves and easing diverge from Go exports.
RemediationProposal: Remove the _sceneSynced gate for evaluation. Initialize Go scene state upon WASM readiness and query Timeline.EvaluateSceneAtTime directly. Retire _evaluateSceneAtTimeJS and duplicate JS bezier math.
RegressionTestRequired: Verify getActiveEngineName() returns 'WASM' on fresh page load without prior project load during playback.

ViolationDescription: Complete parallel JavaScript persistence engine for images, groups, and layers operating when EngineBridge.isReady() is false, creating unanchored objects with local counters that never register in Go.
ActualCallPath: User interaction before WASM ready -> ImageObjects.createImage() -> isReady() is false -> falls through to local array push with image-${this.counter} -> object saved in ImageObjects.list only
FailureScenario: Objects created in JS fallback mode are invisible to Go engine, omitted from SVA packages, ignored by rasterizer exports, and clobbered on subsequent Go scene operations.
RemediationProposal: Reject persistent object creation when Go engine is unready or unavailable. Present a non-interactive loading or error state rather than activating a split-brain in-memory JS editor.
RegressionTestRequired: Verify ImageObjects.createImage returns null and does not mutate ImageObjects.list when EngineBridge.isReady() is false.

ViolationDescription: AppCoordinator.moveSelectedNodes returns true unconditionally without checking the result of EngineBridge.moveGroup or moveNodesGroup, triggering false history recordings and overlay updates even on failure.
ActualCallPath: User drags group -> moveSelectedNodes() -> EngineBridge.moveGroup() returns error -> moveSelectedNodes ignores res -> returns true -> caller records history and shows no error
FailureScenario: Failed Go operations (e.g. locked group or invalid delta) appear successful to UI; history stack records invalid snapshots; UI state diverges from engine state.
RemediationProposal: Check res && res.success in moveSelectedNodes and return false on failure; suppress history recording and show an error notification when Go rejects the operation.
RegressionTestRequired: Verify moveSelectedNodes returns false and does not trigger history recording when EngineBridge.moveGroup returns an error envelope.

ViolationDescription: syncScene constructs a complete scene snapshot by scraping 9 separate global JavaScript lists and dispatches Scene.SetState, which can overwrite newer Go engine scene state.
ActualCallPath: Project apply -> applyStudioState() (projects.js:339) -> syncScene() -> buildCurrentSceneSnapshot() scrapes DOM/lists -> Scene.SetState -> activeScene.SetState()
FailureScenario: If JavaScript lists contain stale or incomplete data (e.g. during partial hydration or unhandled bridge events), Scene.SetState wipes out authoritative Go state.
RemediationProposal: Restrict Scene.SetState strictly to validated project import lifecycles. Ensure project loading decodes directly into Go and hydrates JavaScript via syncFromEngineSnapshot.
RegressionTestRequired: Verify syncScene cannot be called during interactive editing or single-object mutations.

ViolationDescription: Camera, optics, and frame configurations are assembled dynamically in JavaScript by querying DOM form controls (this.getNumControl) rather than maintaining an authoritative Go model.
ActualCallPath: Render cycle -> buildRenderState() -> extracts camera/optics values directly from DOM controls Map -> passes state to Effects.build -> Go engine camera model bypassed
FailureScenario: Camera or optical changes applied in Go or loaded via SVA can be overwritten on the next render cycle by stale DOM control values.
RemediationProposal: Maintain camera, optics, and frame parameters authoritatively in Go; DOM control inputs should dispatch typed update commands, and render states should hydrate from Go snapshots.
RegressionTestRequired: Verify Go camera state changes are reflected in SVG export without being overridden by DOM slider values.

ViolationDescription: Unlayered object fallback rendering in buildFullSVG iterates through Ripples, Glows, Flows, Images, and Nodes that were not in LayerManager and renders them without checking visibility.
ActualCallPath: buildFullSVG() -> renders layered items (checks getEffective) -> enters unlayered loop (lines 435-475) -> directly concatenates render*Element without visibility check
FailureScenario: Objects not indexed in layers (e.g. created prior to layer sync or in unlayered project formats) appear in SVG output even when explicitly marked hidden.
RemediationProposal: Ensure all created objects are registered in Go layer list; add LayerManager.getEffective visibility check to the unlayered fallback loop in buildFullSVG.
RegressionTestRequired: Verify unlayered node with visible: false is omitted from buildFullSVG output.

ViolationDescription: Default photo fit setting is inconsistent across modules: index.html:185 and buildCurrentCanvasState:214 use 'match', while getDefaultControls:508 defines 'contain'.
ActualCallPath: New Blank Project -> ControlStateAdaptor.syncToDOM(getDefaultControls()) sets photoFitSelect to 'contain' -> photo load in projects.js:232 forces 'match'
FailureScenario: Inconsistent canvas framing and letterbox behavior depending on whether a project was loaded, reset, or initialized fresh.
RemediationProposal: Harmonize photoFitSelect default literal to 'match' across getDefaultControls, buildCurrentCanvasState, and index.html.

ViolationDescription: Selection state is mutated optimistically in AppCoordinator.activeSelection before calling Go, and the response from Selection.Set is completely ignored.
ActualCallPath: User clicks object -> selectObject() mutates this.activeSelection -> calls EngineBridge.setSelection() -> ignores return value
FailureScenario: Locked or invalid objects rejected by Go engine remain selected in JavaScript, leading to subsequent command failures or inconsistent UI state.
RemediationProposal: Validate Selection.Set response from Go engine; synchronize activeSelection from Go's authoritative selection response envelope.
RegressionTestRequired: Verify attempting to select a locked object via selectObject is rejected by Go and does not update activeSelection.

ViolationDescription: Image Bake and Commit operations perform multi-step, uncoupled mutations across JS and Go without atomic rollback. commitCurrentCrop ignores bridge return values, and executeBakeImage calls setBackground twice and deletes the image independently.
ActualCallPath: User clicks Bake -> executeBakeImage() -> setLoadedPhoto() -> EngineBridge.setBackground() -> ImageObjects.deleteImage() -> EngineBridge.deleteImage() -> HistoryManager.recordImmediate()
FailureScenario: If setting background fails, image is still deleted; if image deletion fails, background is already replaced; history records corrupted split-brain state.
RemediationProposal: Create an atomic Image.Bake Go command that performs background replacement and image removal in a single revision. Check Go responses in commitCurrentCrop before mutating UI.
RegressionTestRequired: Verify failure during bake background set leaves original image untouched and does not add a history record.

ViolationDescription: LayerManager falls back to _fallbackReorder when EngineBridge.isReady() is false, mutating LayerManager.list locally without updating the Go engine.
ActualCallPath: Layer reorder before WASM ready -> LayerManager._fallbackReorder() mutates this.list -> Go engine layers never updated
FailureScenario: Visual layer order in editor presentation diverges from Go authoritative scene layers and export order.
RemediationProposal: Deprecate _fallbackReorder; all layer modifications must route through Go commands and sync from Go snapshot.
RegressionTestRequired: Verify layer reordering without Go WASM ready returns error rather than mutating local LayerManager.list.

Category: Duplicate Object ID Generation in Fallback Mode
ViolationDescription: JavaScript object modules maintain local counter variables (nodesCounter, flowsCounter) and pre-allocate IDs before calling Go, risking ID collision across nonsequential loads.
ActualCallPath: DiagramNodes.createNode() increments this.counter -> pre-allocates node ID -> sends to Node.Create
FailureScenario: ID collisions with existing objects when projects with nonsequential IDs are loaded, causing Go command rejection.
RemediationProposal: Let Go engine assign authoritative canonical IDs and return created instances to JavaScript adapter.
RegressionTestRequired: Verify Node.Create assigns sequential IDs independent of JS counter.
